assertions.name: orthogonality_holds_at_a6_with_8plus_order_separation
assertions.source: PSD-dominant y_lambda identically 0 under convention D — exact separation, which subsumes the >=1e8 threshold

description: Tests PSD-dominance vs trace-dominance orthogonality at A=6. Mirrors Probe (1) at A=4, which under convention C found PSD-dominant blocks contributing <0.03% of |tr_M|. UNDER CONVENTION D THE RESULT SHARPENS TO AN EXACT ONE: every PSD-dominant shape here has 3 or more rows, and Schur-Weyl on the two-dimensional fibre sends y_lambda to exactly 0 for ell(lambda) >= 3. So the PSD-dominant family contributes IDENTICALLY ZERO, not a small residue, and the separation from the trace-dominant family (1- and 2-row, y ~ 1e-4) is total rather than 9 orders of magnitude. The orthogonality claim survives the convention change and strengthens; it does not dissolve.

magnitude_separation.separation_note: PSD-dominant y_lambda is identically 0 under convention D (every scanned PSD shape has ell(lambda) >= 3, and Schur-Weyl on the two-dimensional fibre sends those to exact zero), so the ratio is infinite and is recorded as null. Under convention C it was a finite ~1e9.

lean_uniqueness_ref.note: T_w uniqueness at the abstract empty-constraint SDP level (PR #1537/#1542 parameterised module). Workplan: docs/workplans/2026-05-31-witness-lean-uniqueness-ref-wiring.md.

caveats: SUPERSEDED UNDER CONVENTION D. This caveat previously read: 'Magnitude separation is a NECESSARY but not sufficient condition for the orthogonality ... rigorous closure needs the tr_M computation', because a 9-OOM gap between a small y_lambda and a large chi^lambda leaves room for a nonzero product. That argument was correct under convention C and does not apply here: the PSD-dominant y_lambda are now EXACTLY 0, so their contribution y_lambda * chi^lambda to tr_M is exactly 0 for any finite chi^lambda. No Hutchinson estimator or diagonal trace is needed to close it — the vanishing is structural (Schur-Weyl on the two-dimensional fibre kills ell(lambda) >= 3), not numerical. What this probe still does NOT establish is anything about the 1- and 2-row trace-dominant family, whose weights are nonzero and whose chi^lambda are not computed here.
